newsitem.title: USA: U.S. broiler production seen up in Q4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. broiler production seen up in Q4.

text.p: U.S. broiler production could rise at least five percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, the Agriculture Department said Wednesday.

In a monthly outlook, the USDA said that placements of broiler chicks has begun to increase significantly compared to last year and are up one to four percent since mid-August. These birds will be slaughtered in early fall.
Wholesale broiler prices are expected to remain strong, despite the higher produciton, supported by strong export demand, USDA said.
Broiler exports are below last year's fast pace, but are seeing rapid growth to China, and growth in other chicken exports are exceeding 1995 levels by a wide margin.
Broiler shipments of 101 million pounds to China have more than doubled in the first seven months of 1996 from last year.
Exports of other chicken products were up three-fold in July from a year earlier, reflecting growth to Canada, Hong Kong and Japan.
September turkey production is expected to increase about six percent, but USDA said negative returns during 1996 are epxected to slow production increases during 1997.
Turkey exports to Russia have soared over the past 18 months, USDA said. Russia is now the second largest export market for U.S. turkey, behind only Mexico.
Exports to Russia in July were 22 million pounds, more than double the previous year and 53 percent of all turkey exports that month. Exports to Russia so far in 1996 have reached 74 million pounds.
USDA said if exports to Russian continue at the current stron pace, it is possible Russia will surpass Mexico as the largest customer of U.S. turkeys.
